html:
In 1976 scientists identified a new and deadly virus during an outbreak at the mission hospital of Yambuku in northern Zaire. They named it after the nearby Ebola river, to avoid giving the village a stigma.

The hospital, run by Belgian nuns, reused a few needles on many patients, which spread the disease. The outbreak killed most of those infected, including several of the nuns. Blood samples were sent to labs in Belgium, Britain and the United States. A team including the young Belgian scientist Peter Piot and experts from the American Centers for Disease Control found a virus related to the Marburg virus and helped stop the outbreak by isolating the sick. A separate outbreak of a related virus struck southern Sudan the same year.

Ebola returned in many later outbreaks. The largest was the West African Ebola epidemic of 2013 to 2016, which killed over 11,000 people and led to the first effective vaccine. Fruit bats are thought to carry the virus. Piot went on to lead the global fight against the AIDS epidemic.
sum: In 1976 scientists identified a new and deadly virus during an outbreak at the mission hospital of Yambuku in northern Zaire. They named it after the nearby Ebola river, to avoid giving the village a stigma.
